parameters.name: code
parameters.value:
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# BUILD_BODY - assemble the Graph sendMail payload safely.
#
# NOTE ON THIS COMMENT BLOCK: variable names are written WITHOUT their
# leading dollar sign. Shuffle substitutes variables everywhere in this
# parameter, comments included - a real dollar reference here would be
# replaced by the error text itself, and a multi-line traceback landing
# mid-comment breaks the node. That would take out alerting for exactly
# the failure you needed to hear about.
#
# WHY THIS NODE EXISTS AT ALL
# The previous approach dropped exec.title and exec.description straight
# into the JSON body of the send node. That works until an error message
# contains a double quote, a backslash or a newline - a Python traceback,
# an echoed HTTP response - at which point the JSON is malformed, the
# send fails, and the alert never arrives. The weirder the failure, the
# more likely it goes unreported. json.dumps() escapes all of it.
#
# THE NEWLINE BEFORE EACH CLOSING TRIPLE-QUOTE IS LOAD-BEARING
# Shuffle substitutes as raw text. A value ending in a double quote would
# sit against the closing delimiter and make four quotes in a row, which
# is a syntax error that kills the node. The newline keeps them apart.
# Do not "tidy" it away.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
import json

title = r"""$exec.title
"""
desc = r"""$exec.description
"""
prefix = r"""$notify_subject_prefix
"""
sender = r"""$notify_from
"""

# --- recipients -------------------------------------------------
try:
    recipients = json.loads(r"""$notify_recipients""")
except Exception:
    recipients = []
if isinstance(recipients, str):
    recipients = [recipients]
recipients = [a.strip() for a in recipients
              if isinstance(a, str) and "@" in a and a.strip()]

# Sending to nobody is worse than sending to the wrong person: it fails
# silently and the workflow still looks healthy.
fallback_used = False
if not recipients:
    recipients = ["gilc@noshut.pt"]
    fallback_used = True

# --- subject ----------------------------------------------------
prefix = " ".join(prefix.split()) or "[Shuffle]"
subject = " ".join((prefix + " " + title).split())[:230]
if fallback_used:
    subject = subject + " (recipient list empty - check notify_recipients)"

# --- body -------------------------------------------------------
content = desc.strip()
if not content:
    content = "(Shuffle sent no description with this notification.)"
if len(content) > 30000:
    content = content[:30000] + "\n\n[truncated by build_body]"

message = {
    "subject": subject,
    "body": {"contentType": "Text", "content": content},
    "toRecipients": [{"emailAddress": {"address": a}} for a in recipients],
}

# Optional From. ONLY works if the identity Shuffle authenticates as holds
# Send As on that mailbox (app token with Mail.Send, or delegated token
# with Mail.Send.Shared plus Send As). Graph rejects the send otherwise,
# so leave notify_from empty unless that is set up.
sender = sender.strip()
if sender and "@" in sender:
    message["from"] = {"emailAddress": {"address": sender}}

# saveToSentItems intentionally NOT set - Graph defaults to true and the
# copy in Sent Items is wanted here.
print(json.dumps({"message": message}))

comments.label: WHY NOT SUBSTITUTE STRAIGHT INTO THE SEND NODE: a quote, backslash or newline in a Shuffle error message breaks the JSON body and the send fails silently - so you stop hearing about exactly the failures that are least routine. json.dumps here escapes all of it. The newline before each closing triple-quote is deliberate too; the code explains why.

UNCHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL except the body parameter. Same auth object, url, headers, ssl_verify and position. saveToSentItems is not set, so Graph keeps its default and the copy still lands in Sent Items.

KEEP THIS WORKFLOW SMALL. It is what tells you every other workflow broke, and nothing watches it in turn - each node added here is another way for it to fail silently. Flood control (suppressing repeats of the same title) was left out for that reason: it needs a cache action and a second failure point.

name: NOSHUT shuffle error email notification
description:
Org notification workflow. Shuffle invokes it with exec.title and exec.description when another workflow errors.

build_body escapes that text with json.dumps and assembles the Graph sendMail payload; the send node posts it unchanged. Substituting the variables straight into the JSON body was the previous approach, and it breaks whenever an error message contains a quote, a backslash or a newline - which is precisely when the alert matters.

SETUP: notify_recipients (JSON array of addresses). Optionally notify_subject_prefix and notify_from. Leave notify_from empty unless the Shuffle identity has Send As on that mailbox.

workflow_variables.description: JSON array of recipient addresses. Change who gets alerted here rather than editing the node body.
workflow_variables.name: notify_recipients

workflow_variables.description: Prefix on every subject so Outlook rules can filter and route these. Defaults to [Shuffle] if left blank.
workflow_variables.name: notify_subject_prefix

workflow_variables.description: Optional From address. ONLY works if the identity Shuffle authenticates as has Send As on that mailbox (app token with Mail.Send, or delegated with Mail.Send.Shared + Send As). Leave empty otherwise - Graph rejects the send.
workflow_variables.name: notify_from
